safePurpose: Explain a non-diagnostic hierarchy for emergency care, same-day malaria testing, and same-day reassessment after negative or pending tests.
privacy: Symptoms, timing, exposure, vulnerability and recent-test selections remain in the current browser page and must not be stored or transmitted.
disallowed: Interpreting a reported test result as a final diagnosis
Recommending antimalarial drugs, prophylaxis choices or doses
Delaying parasite-based testing, reassessment or emergency care
staticText: Malaria Testing Urgency Checklist for /tools/malaria-risk/. Explain only the deterministic non-diagnostic escalation hierarchy. Emergency signs, including inability to keep fluids down, outrank every test or exposure selection. A reported positive result routes to qualified malaria care today. Current symptoms with a negative or pending result route to same-day reassessment because a negative result should be assessed alongside other causes and persistent or worsening symptoms may need professional re-evaluation. Compatible symptoms with possible exposure or higher-risk context prompt same-day parasite-based testing. Geographic or seasonal context cannot diagnose an individual. Do not diagnose or rule out malaria, recommend antimalarial drugs, prophylaxis choices or doses, delay testing or urgent care, or claim real-time local malaria risk. Symptoms and exposure are sensitive and local: do not request names, precise location or identifiers, and do not store, log, upload, sync, email, add selections to URLs or send them to analytics. Sources reviewed 2026-07-26: WHO Malaria fact sheet, WHO Global Malaria Programme diagnosis guidance, and WHO 2025 malaria RDT information notice.
